newsitem.title: UK: Oil price steadies after Friday fall.
newsitem.headline: Oil price steadies after Friday fall.

text.p: World oil prices stabilised on Monday after a heavy sell-off on Friday sparked by a weaker market for heating oil in the United States.
London March futures for international benchmark crude oil Brent blend closed two cents higher at $22.54 a barrel.
In a lethargic session, dealers said they saw the market returning to rangebound trading which it had been trapped in for much of last week.
"The whole market was dying because of that range and now we're back in it again so people don't really know what to do," one broker at London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) said.
Brent fell 66 cents on Friday as dealers liquidated long positions in petroleum products, particularly in U.S. heating oil futures.
Milder than normal weather for the time of year in the U.S. northeast, the world's single largest heating oil market, also helped turn prices lower on Friday.
"The general perception is that the market's moving sideways and seeing whether products will actually hold things up," Harris said.
Analysts said the sideways drift was also a sign of market consolidation.
"The market looks like it wants to consolidate and find its feet and perhaps build a bit of a base before trying to work higher," said Charles Gray, energy analyst at Prudential-Bache in London.
"It may well be that we have to wait until API (U.S. oil stocks data) numbers come out tomorrow night to get a real movement kickstarted here," Gray said.
The American Petroleum Institute figures due for release after futures markets close on Tuesday may provide short-term market direction.
